study: Do credit supply shocks affect fertility choices?
note: Two exogenous shocks (deregulation timing; Bartik IV). D3 moderate: deregulation plausibly moves local income and employment, which the paper addresses but cannot fully rule out.

study: The Babies of Mortgage Market Deregulation
note: Federal regulator ruling gives geographic heterogeneity. D6 moderate: the author's own tests point to ACCESS TO SPACE as the mechanism, which is C.2.c's object even though credit is what varies.

study: Do Mortgage Interest Subsidies Affect Fertility (Taiwan)
note: DiD with matching; FIRST STAGE VERIFIED (mortgage burden -7.9%). The strongest null in the pool.
FE-Poisson + IV, but the instrument is not a policy shock and the first stage is unseen. Abstract-sourced; full text on the residual list.

Randomised, credit arm separately allocated. D5 moderate: contraceptive use did not move much, so for the FP arms the first stage is weak; the credit arm's own first stage is take-up, not contraception. Small magnitudes on a rising-fertility background.
D5 SERIOUS and decisive: the author says the access measures 'are simply too crude', so the null on the bank interaction is uninformative rather than a zero.

study: Fertility and Financial Development, US counties c.1850
note: OLS on a county cross-section; bank presence is not randomly placed. D3 serious: banks locate where commerce is, and commerce moves fertility.

study: Filoso and Papagni, Fertility choice and financial development
note: Cross-country aggregate panel; endogeneity tested for GDP and FLFP only, no instrument for credit.

study: Suriani et al., developed vs developing
note: Two-step system GMM. SARGAN REJECTED (p=0.000) in all 11 models in both samples; Hansen 0.16-0.29. The overidentifying restrictions do not hold.

study: Kuchler, Do Microfinance Programs Change Fertility?
note: DiD on programme participation; participation is self-selected and the paper's own null is on a falling-fertility background.
D1 CRITICAL by the authors' own account: joiners were more educated, married to better-educated men, and MORE LIKELY TO HAVE USED CONTRACEPTIVES BEFORE JOINING. Outcome is desires.

study: Karim et al., NGO membership proxy
note: D1 critical: NGO membership self-selected. D6 moderate: membership is a PROXY for credit receipt.

study: Lan, Pan and Yu, digital financial inclusion
note: Provincial index; D3 serious - digital financial inclusion tracks regional development. Outcome is INTENTIONS.

study: Access to credit and capital markets, China
note: Theory-plus-empirics; the claim extracted is an interaction sign rather than a level effect.
